newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nichiei posts half-year loss on unit's failure.
newsitem.headline: Nichiei posts half-year loss on unit's failure.

text.p: Japanese lumber dealer Nichiei Co Ltd fell into the red because its unit failed earlier this year in Japan's biggest insolvency case since World War Two.

Nichiei announced on Friday that it posted a net loss of 12 billion yen ($108 million) on a parent company basis in the six months to September 30, against a net profit of 215 million yen ($1.93 million) in the same period a year ago.
A huge extraordinary loss stemming from the failure of Nichiei Finance Co Ltd, which had debts of about one trillion yen ($9.0 billion), forced Nichiei Co into the red, the company said.
Nichiei said it expects its parent net loss for the full 1996/97 business year to be 10.7 billion yen ($96.3 million) against a profit of 201 million yen ($1.81 million) in 1995/96.

Nichiei Finance is in the business of property-related financing and is classed as a non-bank financial institution. In October it applied to a court for protection from creditors under Japan's bankruptcy laws.

Like many other Japanese financial institutions, Nichiei Finance has been hit by plummeting real estate prices following the end of Japan's 1980s "bubble economy" of inflated land and stock market prices.

As of the end of September, Nichiei Finance's outstanding borrowings totalled 170.89 billion yen ($1.53 billion) and the debts it had guaranteed totalled 820.65 billion yen ($7.39 billion), making a total of around one trillion yen ($9.0 billion).
The failure of Nichiei Finance pushed up bankruptcy debt in October in Japan to its highest level in a year.

Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co, a private research and rating company, said on Friday that total debt held by bankrupt firms in October nearly doubled from a year ago to 1.36 trillion yen ($12.2 billion). ($1=111 yen)
